features.name: Academic attainment
features.description: The highest formal technical education or degree level the applicant presents as preparation for the role.

levels.descriptor: Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical background only.
Master's degree in computer science or a related technical field.
Doctoral degree in computer science or a related technical field.

features.name: Agentic systems design
features.description: Direct design ownership of agent-based systems, including how autonomy is bounded, supervised, or integrated with backend control infrastructure.

levels.descriptor: No agent-based tooling experience is shown.
The letter mentions agents or autonomous workflows only in general terms.
The letter describes a recognizable agent architecture, typically pairing Python agents with Go services.
The letter shows deliberate control design for agents, such as permissions, auditability, bounded actions, or explicit end-to-end ownership.

features.name: Algorithmic problem solving
features.description: Evidence of practical fluency with data structures and algorithms applied to real engineering problems.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic strength is mentioned.
Claims strong data-structure or algorithm knowledge, but without a concrete example.
Gives at least one concrete example of improving a system through better algorithm or data-structure choice.
Uses a specific, nontrivial example to show strong algorithmic judgment and a meaningful systems improvement.

features.name: Applied AI production experience
features.description: The extent of hands-on experience shipping AI-enabled systems in production, especially with attention to reliability, evaluation, or guardrails.

levels.descriptor: No AI experience is mentioned.
Mentions AI or LLM exposure without concrete deployment detail.
Describes shipped AI features or workflows in production.
Describes shipped AI work plus evaluation, hardening, guardrails, or trustworthiness practices.

features.name: Collaboration posture
features.description: The applicant's willingness and humility to partner closely with security specialists and other internal stakeholders.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention collaboration with security partners.
Implies support for other engineers, but not specifically partnership with security specialists.
Explicitly states readiness to work with security engineers or build for their workflows.
Shows explicit partnership mindset plus concrete evidence of learning from, serving, or collaborating with security specialists.

features.name: Developer enablement philosophy
features.description: Whether the letter frames security engineering as helping developers through better defaults, lower friction, and user-centered tooling.

levels.descriptor: Does not address developer experience or frames security mainly as control.
Shows general willingness to work with developers.
Explicitly emphasizes reducing friction or making secure behavior easier for developers.
Makes developer enablement a central security philosophy and ties examples to that philosophy.

features.name: Evidence specificity
features.description: How concretely the letter supports claims with specific examples, mechanisms, scope, or technical detail.

levels.descriptor: Mostly offers generic assertions or checklist-style requirement matching.
Provides some specifics, but major claims remain abstract or unsubstantiated.
Gives several concrete, role-relevant examples showing what was built or changed.
Repeatedly backs claims with precise mechanisms, context, and outcomes that make the applicant's contribution easy to picture.

features.name: Go fluency
features.description: How central and substantial Go appears in the applicant's professional engineering work.

levels.descriptor: No meaningful Go evidence.
Mentions Go, but without clear depth or ownership.
Shows regular production use of Go in recent work.
Makes Go clearly central, such as a principal language or daily driver tied to sustained backend ownership.

features.name: Impact articulation
features.description: How clearly the letter states the outcomes or effects of the applicant's work, not just responsibilities or technologies.

levels.descriptor: The letter relies mostly on broad claims of fit, skill, or interest without outcomes.
The letter gives some concrete examples of work, but the effect on users, systems, or teams is unclear.
The letter ties accomplishments to visible improvements, such as faster systems, cleaner queues, or reduced manual work.
The letter gives specific accomplishments plus clear operational or organizational outcomes, ideally quantified or sharply contrasted with the prior state.

features.name: Narrative coherence
features.description: Whether the letter forms a connected story or career arc rather than a disconnected list of claims.

levels.descriptor: The letter reads like disconnected bullets, fragments, or stacked claims.
The letter has some structure, but transitions or the overall arc are uneven.
The letter coherently links background, technical experience, and interest in the role.
The letter presents an especially well-shaped narrative that makes the applicant's trajectory and fit feel natural.

features.name: Narrative distinctiveness
features.description: Whether the letter has a memorable voice, opening, or organizing thesis rather than sounding generic.

levels.descriptor: The letter reads like an interchangeable template or a flat list of qualifications.
The letter is competent but generic, with limited individuality in framing or voice.
The letter has a distinctive opening, viewpoint, or sustained framing device.
The letter is memorable and cohesive, with a clear throughline linking the opening idea, past work, and motivation for this role.

features.name: Offensive security practice
features.description: Ongoing attacker-oriented practice outside ordinary development work, such as CTFs or similar exercises.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-practice evidence is mentioned.
Mentions casual or occasional participation with little detail.
Shows regular participation presented as deliberate skill maintenance.
Shows strong results or serious competitive commitment that signals sustained offensive practice.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Responsibility for contributing to or maintaining software used outside the applicant's employer or immediate team.

levels.descriptor: No open-source activity is mentioned.
Mentions occasional patches or minor contributions.
Shows regular contributions or maintainership of a small project.
Maintains a project with outside users or community responsibilities such as reviews, releases, issue handling, or roadmap decisions.

features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: The technical ambition, rigor, and self-directedness of projects built outside formal work.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
The project mentioned is small and mainly serves as lightweight practice or curiosity.
The project shows substantial self-directed engineering with meaningful system design or operational concerns.
The project is an ambitious systems build that tackles hard distributed-systems, storage, or reliability problems.

features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: Motivation for foundational infrastructure or tooling whose benefits compound across many teams or products.

levels.descriptor: No platform or foundational orientation is expressed.
Shows a general desire for impact or infrastructure work, but not strongly.
Clearly expresses a preference for foundational or central platform work.
Makes downstream leverage a primary career motive and connects prior choices to that preference.

features.name: Production delivery track record
features.description: The breadth and depth of hands-on responsibility the applicant shows for testing, maintaining, launching, and operating real production software systems.

levels.descriptor: Only one or two launched or maintained services are mentioned, or the scope is vague.
Roughly three or four services are mentioned, showing repeated production ownership.
Five or more services are mentioned, with explicit launch, maintenance, or testing responsibility.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: How concretely and seriously the letter shows Python as a real production language for services, tooling, automation, or agents.

levels.descriptor: Python is absent or appears only incidentally.
Python is mentioned as a tool or companion language, but depth is unclear.
The letter shows regular production Python use for tooling, automation, prototypes, or services.
Python is portrayed as a major production language with broad, concrete use across services, automation, and agent behavior.

features.name: Relevant software tenure
features.description: The amount of directly relevant professional software-engineering time the applicant claims.

levels.descriptor: Below the role minimum or unclear on relevant experience length.
Roughly meets the minimum, around 2 to 3 years of relevant experience.
Shows solid mid-level experience, around 4 to 5 years.
Shows strong experience depth, around 6 or more years.

features.name: Reliability and maintainer mindset
features.description: Emphasis on rigor, maintainability, careful operation, testing, resilience, and long-term ownership over pure feature shipping.

levels.descriptor: Shows little sign of care for maintainability, testing, or long-term operation.
Mentions maintenance or correctness only generically.
Explicitly emphasizes dependable systems, careful engineering, or maintainer habits.
Shows multiple reinforcing signals such as typed or tested tooling, careful releases, production standards, or pride in quiet reliability.

features.name: Role-specific fit and motivation
features.description: How specifically and convincingly the letter explains why this exact role or team fits the applicant's background, interests, and mission.

levels.descriptor: The motivation is formulaic and could fit almost any software-engineering application.
The letter shows some interest in security or Google, but the rationale is still fairly generic.
The letter gives clear, role-relevant motivation tied to the team's mission, working model, or problem space.
The letter gives memorable, well-tailored motivation that shows the applicant has thought specifically about this team's security-automation challenge.

features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: The depth of hands-on experience assessing systems for security weaknesses and following findings through remediation.

levels.descriptor: No security assessment work is mentioned.
Mentions security reviews or assessments only in general terms.
Describes concrete assessment work such as threat models, design reviews, or attack-surface analysis.
Shows repeated, substantive assessment work with follow-through such as documented findings, remediation validation, or attacker-style code reading.

features.name: Security automation insight
features.description: Understanding of the role as a systems problem of scaling scarce security expertise through automation and security-at-scale tooling.

levels.descriptor: The letter shows little understanding of the specific security problem this team solves.
The letter shows general interest in security engineering, but mostly at a broad level.
The letter clearly articulates goals like reducing manual security work or making the secure path easier for developers.
The letter shows nuanced insight into bottlenecks such as scarce expert attention, vulnerability triage, lifecycle embedding, bounded agents, or similar operational realities.

features.name: Security credential strength
features.description: The presence and rigor of formal external security certifications or credentials.

levels.descriptor: No relevant security certification is stated.
A baseline or survey credential such as Security+ is stated.
A rigorous hands-on credential such as OSCP or a similarly demanding practical certification is stated.

features.name: Vulnerability triage automation
features.description: Experience automating vulnerability-report intake, classification, routing, deduplication, prioritization, or related security workflows.

levels.descriptor: No past vulnerability-handling automation is mentioned.
The letter expresses interest in this problem, but gives no concrete example of having automated it.
A concrete example of triage, intake, routing, or report-handling automation is described.
The letter shows strong end-to-end automation of vulnerability handling, with clear workflow transformation or operational value.

features.name: Writing polish
features.description: The surface professionalism and readability of the letter, including spelling, grammar, proofreading, and copy accuracy.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors, misspellings, or naming mistakes noticeably distract from the application.
Several noticeable errors appear, but the letter remains readable.
Mostly clean writing with only minor slips.
Polished, professional, and essentially error-free throughout.

other.name: Other
other.description: Idiosyncratic or sparsely recurring constructs that do not fit the larger shared criteria, such as extra language breadth, generic security reasoning, or claimed autonomy level.

levels.descriptor: No additional languages are mentioned.
Mentions 1 to 2 additional languages.
Mentions 3 to 5 additional languages.
Mentions more than 5 additional languages.
